title: Convolutions & Computer Vision
why: Vision is a core ML specialty and a clear demonstration of how architecture encodes assumptions about data.
explain: A convolution slides a small learned filter over an image, taking a dot product at each position. Because the same filter is reused everywhere, a CNN needs far fewer parameters than a fully connected network and detects a pattern wherever it appears. Early layers learn edges, later layers learn parts and objects.

Pooling downsamples feature maps and adds tolerance to small shifts. The output size along each dimension is floor((n + 2p - k) / s) + 1 for input size n, kernel k, padding p and stride s. Batch normalization, dropout and data augmentation (flips, crops, color jitter) fight overfitting.

In practice you rarely train from scratch. Transfer learning starts from a network pretrained on a large dataset (for example ResNet on ImageNet), freezes or fine-tunes some layers, and often beats a from-scratch model that used ten times more of your own data.
key_points: Weight sharing gives translation equivariance and few parameters
Transfer learning: freeze the backbone, train the head, then fine-tune carefully
Evaluate on images that look like production, not just the benchmark
pitfalls: Data leakage through near-duplicate images across the train/validation split
Augmentations that change the label (for example flipping digits or text)

leetcode.why: Flood fill is region growing, a basic image-segmentation operation.
Measuring connected-component size is how you count and size objects in a mask.
The integral image (2D prefix sum) answers region queries in O(1) and underpins classic detectors.
Multi-source BFS computes a distance transform over an image grid.
Updating each cell from its neighborhood is the same access pattern as a convolution.

industry.q: A conv layer takes a 32x32x3 input and uses 16 filters of size 5x5 with stride 1 and padding 2. What are the output shape and the parameter count?
key_points: Padding 2 with a 5x5 kernel keeps the spatial size ('same')

industry.q: You have 500 labeled images. How do you build a good classifier?
key_points: Transfer learning from a pretrained model
Freeze the backbone first, then fine-tune with a small learning rate

industry.q: A vision model works in the lab but fails on phone photos. Why might that happen?
key_points: Distribution shift: lighting, blur, resolution, framing
Augment to resemble production and collect real samples
